cohort: 230 mothers (115 in the C-section group and 115 in the vaginal delivery group) who delivered within the past six months.
finding: Vaginal delivery was associated with shorter recovery times, lower pain scores, lower postpartum depression prevalence, and better quality of life compared to C-section.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery was associated with faster recovery and better psychological outcomes compared to C-section.
cross-section timing: Data was collected within six months postpartum.
